title: The moderns: operating grace produces undeliberate movements
source_text: XLIV. Verum hodierni plerique Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores, per gratiam operantem intelligunt, eam per quam in nobis producuntur illi animi motus, qui sunt indeliberati, & a Libero consensu voluntatis nostrae non pendent. Quales sunt piae cogitationes, & mentis illustrationes, & etiam pia quaedam desideria, quibus a Deo movemur atque sollicitamur ad fidem & conversionem.
pass_a_gloss: XLIV. But most present-day Doctors of the Roman Church, by operating grace understand, that through which in us are produced those motions of the soul, which are undeliberated, and do not depend on the free consent of our will. Such are pious thoughts, and illuminations of the mind, and also certain pious desires, by which we are moved by God and solicited to faith and conversion.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLIV. Most present-day doctors of the Roman Church, however, take operating grace to mean the grace by which those movements of the soul are produced in us that are undeliberate and do not depend on our will's free consent.
These are devout thoughts, enlightenments of the mind and also certain devout desires, by which God moves and urges us toward faith and conversion.
